cards.front: Bonding is not a complete property prediction
cards.back: Bonding models constrain likely interactions, but composition, defects, microstructure, processing and environment also shape measured properties.
Metals, ceramics, polymers and composites are useful organizing classes; a class name does not specify exact stiffness, toughness or degradation.
Density = mass/volume; ideal layer R = L/(kA); percent increase uses the initial value as denominator. Show units and model boundaries.
For a plane, take axis-intercept reciprocals in lattice units, clear fractions and reduce. Parentheses denote planes; square brackets denote directions.
d(hkl) = a/√(h²+k²+l²). The same convention and units must be used for a, d and wavelength.
First-order nλ = 2d sinθ relates wavelength, spacing and θ. Report θ or 2θ explicitly; one peak does not establish complete phase identity.
Vacancies and substitutions are point defects, dislocations are line defects, and grain boundaries/interfaces are planar defects; their mechanisms differ.
D = D₀exp(−Q/RT) is an Arrhenius model. Flux magnitude in a steady 1D gradient is DΔC/Δx, with sign set by coordinates.
Solid solution, grain refinement, work and precipitation strengthening can raise resistance to deformation while changing ductility or other properties.
In a two-phase tie-line field, each phase fraction uses the opposite tie-line arm; fractions sum to one and composition conventions must match.
A phase has structural/compositional identity; a microconstituent is an organized region that can contain multiple phases.
History can change transformation fractions, scale and defects. Equilibrium diagrams do not supply transformation time or a heat-treatment recipe.
Strength describes stress capacity under a defined condition; toughness relates to energy absorption. Stress–strain area is a model-dependent toughness proxy.
Creep is time-dependent deformation, fatigue accumulates cyclic damage, and fracture models connect stress, flaw size and geometry with limitations.
Galvanic coupling and passive-film stability depend on environment and area; pitting and crevice attack are localized and not ruled out by passivity.
Mn is chain-count weighted, Mw is mass weighted, and PDI = Mw/Mn. For a nonuniform population Mw exceeds Mn; all are distribution summaries.
Tg concerns amorphous-segment mobility and Tm crystalline melting. Semicrystalline polymers can exhibit both; ceramics need separate microstructure analysis.
Voigt is arithmetic stiffness mixing and Reuss harmonic mixing under idealized assumptions. Orientation, interfaces and flaws still require evidence.
First compute d = λ/[2sin(θ)] for first order, then a = d√(h²+k²+l²) for the stipulated cubic assignment.
Mass loss = (initial − final)/initial × 100. It quantifies change but does not identify the lost species or mechanism.
A blank thermal event is not zero and must not be copied from another sample. Multi-technique agreement does not erase alternatives.
Declare hard eligibility constraints first, then compare eligible candidates using documented criteria; do not hide a failed requirement inside a weighted score.
E/ρ requires consistent SI units. Fixed-volume mass = ρV and modeled embodied energy = mass × energy intensity.
A synthetic selection can be conditionally eligible only within its model. Fatigue, joining, standards and application-specific reviews remain open.
